query: What do Samsung Galaxy S7 owners report about camera quality, including blurry shots or photos in low light?
search_text: What do owners report about camera quality, including blurry shots or photos in low light?

rows.text: My small testing of this showed improvements in picture quality of low light in about half of the pictures I took. The best improvement is in room lighting where it is dimmed mood lighting near you, and then the area in the distance also has some dimmed lighting. The close area is represented well in the picture and so is the other area that has its own lighting. Other pictures that didn't do so well had only one source of dimmed lighting. But my favorite feature of the camera is its speed. I often take pictures of groups of people and I take many rapid-fire shots at a time in the hopes that I will get one or two pictures where everyone has the right expression and looking in the right direction.

Actually I felt my phone took better pictures than I could with my DSLR and the lenses I own at the Aquarium(I'm sure if I had more expensive lenses that take fast photos in low light it would be better). Also love the beauty mode laugh It has some great settings and I absolutely love it! I'm including some photos I took with it.

Camera In a word, it sucks compared to the Motorola or even my iPhone 7. Compared to other phones (iPhone 6, etc.), it's okay. It has a hard time finding proper focal points in some situations, like when shooting through glass. It is also very background focus dependent. When shooting a small subject with a complex background, it rarely focuses on the primary subject. Tapping the screen to manually select the focal point seemingly locks on then drifts away a moment later. I would estimate that 50% of my shots are not fully in focus as a result. I never had this issue with the Motorola, or any of my iPhones. Fortunately the stock camera app does allow for quite a bit of control which helps to overcome the focus issues. Video's are very nice and shooting in 4K is great.

Nice but Not Reliable. When the phone works, it does quite well. The camera is very good and the ability to connect calls is average. This is happening more and more frequently and is very annoying. My Galaxy S6 got just a little liquid near it and was destroyed. I am finished buying Samsung products, as the quality is suspect.

I have been getting great indoor (and outdoor) shots of my 5-year old in action. With my old phone, that was completely impossible since it would take at least 10 seconds to open the camera app and focus. With the S7, I can go from picking up the locked phone to capturing a perfectly focused image in 3 seconds (I caught my son in mid-air as he jumped off a ramp on his scooter). And the colors are almost always very close to what I perceive with my eye, even in some unusual lighting (like midnight in the arctic in spring, or mixed fluorescent light/sunlight in my living room). The screen is gorgeous as everyone knows. Its resolution is riDONKulous. The phone is a good size for me (good balance between being comfortable in the hand, fitting in the pocket, and having a usefully sized screen).

looking like it was struck by a bb. Samsung has a serious issue they are trying to avoid in the wake of the NOTE 7 debacle. A quick google of S7 rear camera reveals the issue is with the whole S7 gen phones. Thousands of people are reporting the rear camera glass shattering, looking like it was struck by a bb, and rendering the camera and the default camera app unless, while the phone sitting untouched, in their pocket or even while taking a picture. According to samsung reps, this is physical damage caused by the user. There is either a large batch of defective camera/camera lenses, or something in the phone is heating up, causing expansion, pushing against the camera lens and causing it to shatter. Samsung obviously can't afford to have this get out and keeps pushing the user issue narrative.
